title: Unmeasured Zero-Copy Lifetime Infection
pattern: Prematurely declaring struct fields as borrowed references (`&'a str`, `&'a [u8]`) rather than owned values (`String`, `Vec<u8>`) to achieve "zero-copy performance."
why_bad: It infects the entire codebase with complex lifetime parameters, making structs highly un-composable and difficult to maintain. The time spent by programmers fighting lifetime errors and code complexity far exceeds the negligible cost of cloning a small string [100, 235, 319].
detection: The extensive use of lifetime annotations (`'a`) throughout data models, structs, and database entities whose only purpose is holding textual name or reference strings.
fix: Store owned values (`String`, `Vec<u8>`) directly in data model structs, or use `std::sync::Arc` or `std::borrow::Cow` if reference sharing is strictly necessary under profiled scenarios.
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 20 (p. 319); *Software Design for Flexibility*, Chapter 1 (p. 100); *Refactoring to Patterns*, Chapter 1 (p. 235).
